entities.summary:
Rudolf of Mecklenburg-Stargard (died 1415) was a prominent ecclesiastical figure in late medieval Northern Europe, serving successively as Bishop of Skara in Sweden and then as Bishop of Schwerin within the Holy Roman Empire. A scion of the ducal House of Mecklenburg, his career illustrates the intricate intertwining of aristocratic lineage, ecclesiastical power, and regional political maneuvering characteristic of the era. His tenure saw him navigate the complexities of the Great Western Schism and the ambitions of powerful secular rulers, positioning him as a key, albeit often contested, spiritual and temporal authority across significant swathes of the Baltic littoral.

Initially elected Bishop of Skara in 1386, Rudolf's appointment was confirmed by Pope Urban VI, aligning him with the Roman obedience during the Great Western Schism. His time in Sweden was marked by efforts to assert episcopal authority amidst ongoing conflicts between the Danish monarchy (then ruling Sweden through Margaret I) and local Swedish nobles. Transferring to the more politically central See of Schwerin in 1390, a move also confirmed by the Roman pope, Rudolf established his primary residence in Bützow. Here, he diligently administered his diocese, overseeing church lands, mediating local disputes, and participating in provincial synods, consolidating the temporal and spiritual influence of the bishopric against the backdrop of a fragmented Holy Roman Empire.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rudolf of Mecklenburg-Stargard was a notable regional ecclesiastical figure, stabilizing two bishoprics during the Great Western Schism and preserving the temporal influence of the Schwerin See. His career offers insight into the intersection of noble lineage and church authority in late medieval Northern Europe.
